By contrast, in imaginary concurrence, Article 40 of the Criminal Act requires punishment according to the heaviest penalty prescribed for the most serious offense, so the person would always be punished by death, life imprisonment, or imprisonment without labor under Article 88, which makes no balance with Article 87(2), which prescribes imprisonment or imprisonment without labor for at least 5 years. In light of this, in this case the lower court, while describing the acts of Defendants D, E, F, and G as those of persons engaged in important duties in the riot constituting insurrection, nevertheless applied to them the offense of murder with insurrectionary purpose and punished them by the heavier penalty of murder with insurrectionary purpose. This amounts to a case where the application of law was wrong and it affected the judgment. Therefore, I cannot agree with the majority opinion that maintains such lower judgment, and the lower judgment should also be reversed on this point.

5. Supreme Court Justice Jeong Tae-won’s opinion

This is the same as part (2) of the opinion of Supreme Court Justice Seo Yun-hong below concerning Defendants E and F, and part (3) concerning Defendant G.

6. Supreme Court Justice Seo Yun-hong’s opinion

In view of the facts and evidence in this case, I cannot agree with the majority opinion that would maintain the lower judgment finding all charges against Defendants C, E, F, and G guilty for the following reasons.

(1) As to Defendant C

First, regarding the offense of murder by conspiracy co-principal liability against this Defendant, the point of the lower court, the Army High Military Court, in finding this guilty is ultimately that the Defendant conspired with co-defendant A to kill the deceased T, the President’s security chief, and although he did not directly act, he caused A to carry out the killing and thus achieved the purpose. The supporting facts and evidence are summarized as follows: two hours before the shooting as execution of the murder by A, when the Defendant met A at the curb in the garden at the entrance to the Gungjeong-dong office, the Blue House branch of the Central Intelligence Agency, A said “I will get rid of the chief T,” and the Defendant nodded; he did not restrain A’s conduct at the shooting scene; and later that day, when the situation developed and Defendant met A in the restroom of the Army Headquarters banka and rebuked him, saying “Why did you even kill the President?”, from these things it was inferred that he intended the gunshot killing of T.

However, the so-called conspiracy co-principal liability is a concept concerning an execution principal. In light of social reality, in crimes by multiple persons there are cases where the substantive principal plans the crime behind the scenes and causes the execution act to be carried out by subordinates or persons under the principal’s control, and in such cases simple instigation or aiding and abetting is not enough. This theory emerged from judicial necessity. Even in such cases, the substantive principal must have the subjective intent to commit the crime as his own. Merely inducing another’s intent or tolerating or using another’s crime does not fall within this category. In this case, the lower court’s reasoning concerning Defendant C and the supporting facts are plainly not of that nature. No one can deny that the true subject of this shocking offense of assassinating the President was A, not Defendant C, but it is hard to understand that only with respect to the part of killing T the Defendant is treated as the principal and A as the executor under Defendant’s direction. Even if it is true that the Defendant nodded when A said get rid of him, that would, at most, mean he tolerated murder, and it is unclear why that can become a joint plot to kill. Likewise, even if he did not restrain A at the scene of the killing, that was merely passivity toward murder. More inexplicable still, the fact that the chief secretary Defendant did not restrain the shooting death of the President at the scene is not reproached in this case, yet failing to restrain the killing of the security chief is treated as conspiracy co-principal liability for murder. Also, the conversation in the Army banka restroom with A as a post hoc support for the plot is hard to accept when the plot itself is a major fact requiring strict proof.

Second, as to the attempted insurrection offense against the same Defendant, insurrection is a crime under Article 87 of the Criminal Act with the purpose of subverting the Constitution, and the concrete content of the Constitution at issue in this case is that the constitutional order was to be changed by assassinating the President. Therefore, whether Defendant had the intent to assassinate the President is indispensable for recognizing the purpose of insurrection against him.

However, at the time of filing the original indictment, it was stated as a factual allegation that Defendant also conspired with A to assassinate the President, but this part of the indictment was later amended in the lower court, and the lower court’s factual findings also finalized that Defendant had no relation to the assassination of the President. Therefore, attempted major participation in insurrection cannot be established against Defendant. Although the record suggests some doubt that on the day of the incident Defendant may have, in the sequence of acts he performed until A was arrested, either cooperated with A’s conspiracy or aided it, that doubt arises only from inference and circumstances. Since insurrection is a crime with a specific purpose, the evidence or facts to establish that purpose are major facts requiring strict proof. Thus, the fact that Defendant did not immediately report A after the crucial shooting cannot be deemed a suspicious circumstance from which it reflexively follows that he participated in the major duties of insurrection. Especially given the situation at the time, there was no guarantee that Defendant himself would not be shot by A. To say that merely because he did not disclose A’s offense until four hours after the assassination, when reporting to the Minister of National Defense and the Army Chief of Staff, he did so for the purpose of insurrection is a leap in logic. Moreover, in this case, where no one can deny that A’s attempt at insurrection failed because of Defendant’s report, it is not proper under the principle of fairness to infer from the reporting fact a basis unfavorable to the Defendant and thereby convict him.

Therefore, as to Defendant C, I cannot agree with the majority opinion that would maintain the lower judgment, which does not establish the several decisive circumstances set forth above. The grounds of appeal on these points are meritorious.

(2) As to Defendants E and F

The lower judgment finding these Defendants guilty of attempted insurrection and murder with insurrectionary purpose also cannot be left standing. It is undeniable that, as co-defendants and subordinates of D, they shot and killed U and X, security guards of the Presidential Security Service, while staying at the Gungjeong-dong intelligence restaurant on the day of the offense. However, for that act to be murder with insurrectionary purpose, there must be awareness of the insurrectionary purpose, namely subversion of the Constitution. On this point, the only materials the lower court or the majority opinion regarded as evidence are the statements the Defendants made during the military investigation. Their statements merely amount to saying they thought that if things went well, they would be promoted or get a share. To say that those statement entries are sufficient evidence that they knew of subversion of the Constitution, i.e. the assassination of the President, and participated in the offense exceeds the bounds of free conviction.

As to how those statements were made, the record shows they were the result of leading questions and inferences made by the military investigative authorities, so one cannot distinguish whether they are opinions or statements of fact. It is hard to understand how they can be linked to awareness of the assassination of the President or subversion of the Constitution. Regarding the circumstances by which the Defendants came to shoot, co-defendant D merely instructed them to drive the security guards in the restaurant into a corner and, if they resist, return fire. Defendant F was D’s driver, and E was also a guard at Gungjeong-dong with little education. Even if one has difficulty asking them about the meaning of subverting the Constitution, the minimum would be awareness of the assassination of the President. Yet there is no clear material in this case showing even that awareness on their part. To uphold a death sentence by recognizing that all of this existed is unacceptable.

(3) As to Defendant G

This Defendant is recognized by the lower court as having committed attempted insurrection and murder with insurrectionary purpose by carrying out so-called confirmation killing 30 minutes after the gunfire in this case, thereby completely extinguishing the lives of T and U, who were still alive at the time. This part also cannot be left standing.

The time of the above confirmation killing by the Defendant is fixed by the lower court as 20:05 on that day, whereas the shooting of Chief T by A was at 19:40. Then it is difficult, in view of the various materials, to conclude that even 25 to 30 minutes after the first shot T was still groaning and had not died. On that day A shot T, then fired at the President, and shortly thereafter hid in the restroom, then fired the final shot into T’s abdomen and again shot the President; the record and the lower court both accept this. Then T’s time of death would have been at least before, or at the same time as, the President’s death. The hospital authorities stated that the President’s time of death was five minutes before the time the body was transported to the military hospital, that is, before 19:57 that day. In the end, if the President’s time of death can be estimated as 10 to 12 minutes after A’s first shooting, then T’s time of death would also be 19:50 or 19:52. Then it would be reasonable to conclude that at the time of Defendant G’s confirmation killing at 20:05, the victim T had already died. Otherwise, because the autopsy report and photographs of the body are in the record and the exact location of the gunshot wounds is clearly shown, the court should have had an expert assess the time of death and conducted a hearing accordingly.

Nevertheless, without taking such measures, to recognize murder with insurrectionary purpose and even impose the death penalty merely on the Defendant’s statement that T seemed to be making some sound at the time of the confirmation killing is utterly incomprehensible. Therefore, failing to examine this point and determine whether it was murder or merely a gunshot at a corpse amounts to a failure of hearing or defect for lack of reasons. Moreover, the record does not show where or what the Defendant was doing before the confirmation killing. To recognize guilt for insurrection on the ground that the killing was for an insurrectionary purpose is also not free from the criticism of finding facts without evidence.

For these reasons, I cannot agree with the majority opinion that would maintain the Army High Military Court judgment on Defendants C, E, F, and G, and I state that the grounds of appeal on these points are meritorious.

{"[88DO650]": "The grounds of appeal filed by the Defendants and by the court-appointed defense counsel are 함께 판단된다

Based on the evidence adopted by the judgment of the court of first instance, which the court below affirmed, the court below found that Defendant <REDACTED> had long harbored intense 불만 over the victim <REDACTED> teasing the wife of the co-defendant, who was somewhat 저능아였던, by asking her for breast milk, and that, on 1987. 8. 8. around 23:30, while drinking with the victim at the village store in <REDACTED>, Goesan County, Chungcheongbuk-do, he heard from the owner of said store, non-party <REDACTED>, that even during the daytime of that day the victim had teased the wife of the co-defendant by asking her for breast milk, whereupon he struck the victim’s cheeks several times and otherwise assault했다. Thereafter, as the three of them, namely Defendant <REDACTED>, who had come there, the victim, and Defendant <REDACTED>, were heading together to a nearby <REDACTED> in order to drink more liquor, when they reached the farm road in front of the village, the victim, who was in a state of heavy intoxication, made a gesture with his fingers as if to gouge out their eyes and used abusive language, such as saying, “If this bastard keeps fooling around, I will kill him,” whereupon Defendant <REDACTED> struck the victim’s cheeks several times with the palm of his hand, and Defendant <REDACTED> also struck the victim’s abdomen twice, causing the victim to fall down. Then, in a moment of erupting anger, they resolved to kill the victim, and Defendant <REDACTED> climbed onto the victim’s body and struck the victim’s chest twice with a stone measuring 20 centimeters in width and 10 centimeters in length (Prosecution Exhibit No. 1), and Defendant <REDACTED> likewise joined in and struck the victim’s head twice with a stone measuring 13 centimeters in width and 7 centimeters in length (Prosecution Exhibit No. 2). Thereafter, they again raised the victim to his feet, and Defendant <REDACTED> struck the victim’s abdomen once, causing him to fall backward; and when the victim lost consciousness and went limp due to concussion and the like, they mistook him for dead and, for the purpose of secretly burying the corpse and destroying evidence, dragged the victim to a stream about 150 meters away from there, dug a pit with a shovel, and buried the victim, thereby causing the victim to die of suffocation. Upon comparing this with the record, the above finding is proper, and there is no illegality in having erred in fact-finding by violating the rules of logic and experience in evaluating evidence, as alleged in the grounds. Further, even if, as stated above, the victim did not directly die from the assault committed by the Defendants with intent to kill, but instead died from the burial conducted for the purpose of destroying the traces of the crime, if the entire course is viewed comprehensively, the initially foreseen fact of the victim’s killing was ultimately realized, and the Defendants cannot escape criminal liability for homicide; accordingly, the court below’s decision, in the same sense, to uphold the first-instance judgment convicting the Defendants of homicide is proper, and there is no error whatsoever therein

Further, according to the record, it is recognized that Defendant <REDACTED> was somewhat intoxicated at the time of the above offense, but it does not appear that, as a result, said Defendant had reached the level of diminished mental and physical capacity; therefore, the argument on this point is also without merit

In addition, in this case, in which a sentence of less than 10 years’ imprisonment was imposed, the argument that the court below’s sentencing is too severe cannot constitute a lawful ground for appeal in light of Article 383, item 4, of the Criminal Procedure Act. All of the grounds are without merit

Therefore, the appeals of the Defendants are all dismissed, and each Defendant shall have a portion of the days of detention after appeal credited toward the principal sentence, and the judgment is rendered as stated in the Disposition by unanimous opinion of the Justices participating

question: 압수 · search에 관한 설명 중 incorrect한 것을 모두 고른 것은? (In cases of dispute, pursuant to case law) ㄱ. 피압수자가 investigative agency에 압수․search warrant의 execution에 participate하지 않는다는 의사를 명시하였다면 special circumstances가 있는 경우를 제외하고는 그 defense counsel에게 압수․search warrant의 execution에 참여할 기회를 separately 보장하지 않아도 무방하다. ㄴ. investigative agency가 범죄 혐의사실과 관련 있는 information을 selectively 압수한 후에도 그와 관련이 없는 나머지 information을 delete · discard · return하지 아니한 채 그대로 retain하고 있다면 범죄 혐의사실과 관련이 없는 부분에 대하여는 the scope of electronic information subject to seizure를 넘어서는 electronic information을 warrant 없이 압수 · search하여 obtained한 것이어서 unlawful하고, later에 court로부터 압수 · search warrant가 issued되었다거나 defendant나 defense counsel이 이를 evidence로 함에 consent하였다고 하여 그 illegality가 cured된다고 볼 수 없다. ㄷ. information storage medium을 voluntary submitted한 피압수자에 더하여 voluntary submitter 아닌 suspect에게도 participation right가 guaranteed되어야 하는 ‘ 피의자의 소유 · management에 속하는 information storage medium ’ 란, suspect가 압수 · search 당시 또는 이와 temporally proximate한 시기까지 해당 information storage medium을 actually controlled · managed하면서 그 information storage medium 내 electronic information 전반에 관한 exclusive management and disposal authority를 possessed · exercised하고, otherwise 이를 자신의 의사에 따라 third party에게 transferred하거나 relinquished하지 아니한 경우로서, suspect를 그 information storage medium에 stored된 electronic information에 대하여 substantive person subject to seizure로 평가할 수 있는 경우를 말한다. ㄹ. substantive person subject to seizure에 해당하는지 여부는 압수 · search 당시 externally · objectively recognizable한 factual condition을 기준으로 판단하여야 하는바, suspect나 other third party가 과거 그 information storage medium의 use 내지 individual electronic information의 creation · use 등에 involved한 사실이 있다거나 그 과정에서 created된 electronic information에 의해 identified되는 data subject에 해당한다는 사정이 있다면 그들을 substantively 압수 · search를 받는 party로 treat하여야 한다. ㅁ. suspect가 mobile phone을 voluntary submitting하면서 mobile phone에 저장된 electronic information이 아닌 cloud 등 third party가 managed하는 remote location에 stored되어 있는 electronic information을 investigative agency에 제출한다는 의사로 investigative agency에게 cloud 등에 access하기 위한 ID와 password를 voluntary provided하였다면 위 cloud 등에 stored된 electronic information을 voluntary submission하는 것으로 볼 수 있다.
